title: Distributed dual-comb spectroscopy
authors: Haowei Shi, Kartikeya Arora, Zheshen Zhang, Quntao Zhuang
abstract: We propose distributed dual-comb spectroscopy, a quantum-enhanced sensing architecture that simultaneously exploits spatial- and spectral-domain entanglement to improve the extraction of global spectroscopic information across broadband frequency ranges. Our scheme consists of a network of Mach-Zehnder interferometers interrogating spatially separated samples, each driven by a classical frequency comb at the bright port. A single two-mode squeezed frequency comb is distributed through a passive beam-splitter array into $K$ entangled combs, establishing multipartite correlations across sensors while preserving intrinsic spectral entanglement. The protocol is compatible with both heterodyne detection and division detection, and enables parallel estimation of weighted-average absorption features over multiple frequency components. Compared with spatially separable quantum strategies requiring $K$ independently engineered nonclassical comb sources, our approach achieves enhanced signal-to-noise performance using only a single quantum resource distributed across the network. These results establish a scalable route toward broadband distributed quantum spectroscopy with simultaneous spatial and spectral advantage.
summary: This paper introduces distributed dual-comb spectroscopy, a quantum-enhanced sensing technique that uses a single distributed squeezed frequency comb across multiple interferometers. It theoretically demonstrates that this approach significantly improves the signal-to-noise ratio for measuring global spectroscopic properties compared to classical or independently sourced quantum methods. The work establishes a scalable quantum route for broadband, multi-site sensing.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the extraction of global spectroscopic information across broadband frequency ranges by simultaneously exploiting spatial and spectral entanglement in distributed sensing.
main_result: The proposed distributed quantum spectroscopy scheme achieves enhanced signal-to-noise performance using only a single distributed quantum resource, outperforming spatially separable quantum strategies.
method: The analysis uses quantum optical techniques involving two-mode squeezed frequency combs distributed across a network of Mach-Zehnder interferometers (MZIs) to model and estimate weighted-average absorption features.
model_or_system: The physical platform is distributed dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) utilizing a network of MZIs interrogating multiple, spatially separated samples ($K$). The core quantum resource is a single two-mode squeezed frequency comb distributed via a passive beam-splitter array.
key_observables: Mean and noise terms for the detected signal ($\hat{d}_m$ and $\Delta\hat{d}_m$), and the estimator $\hat{	heta}$ for the weighted average of absorption features.
important_parameters: The number of samples ($K$), the quantum squeezing level, and the relative weights ($w(\ell)$) assigned to different spatial locations.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the weak absorption limit ($	au \simeq 1$) for simplicity, and treats the local oscillator comb semi-classically.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the DCS setup with heterodyne and quantum comb interferometry. Figure 2 shows the setup for $K$-sample gas-gradient sensing, and Figure 3 illustrates the setup for estimating averages of multiple gases.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by modeling the quantum light interaction in the MZI, deriving the mean and noise for the estimator, and then optimizing the power allocation and readout scheme (comparing heterodyne vs. division detection) to minimize the variance for estimating global parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed quantum-enhanced measurement protocol for distributed sensing, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, particularly in developing scalable quantum sensors.
